On Tue, Aug 19, 2014 at 5:11 PM, Roger Billig <rogerb...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Dr.  Nicholas J. Matzke,

I have a small question regarding a figure in your new paper in Systematic Biology (http://sysbio.oxfordjournals.org/content/early/2014/08/14/sysbio.syu056.full.pdf+html). Regarding Figure 1., I was wondering if the DEC model covers only the grey cladogenesis events, does the DEC+J model cover all of the rest or only the first and last columns ? 


Hi, DEC+J covers the grey cladogenesis events (the same as DEC), adding only those in the right column (founder events).


 


You can also see my question in this manner, does the DEC+J cover for example :
1) the Sympatric subset event ABCD (ancestor) into AB (daughter 1) and ABCD (daughter 2) or
 
 
This event is impossible under both DEC and DEC+J.

 

 
2) the vicariance event ABCD (ancestor) into AB (daughter 1) and CD (daughter 2).

This is impossible under both DEC and DEC+J, as these models rule vicariance with two widespread daughters. DIVALIKE would allow this event, however.
 

I am also asking you this question because after consulting Table 1a and 1b it is still not clear to me.

The thing to focus on there is the ancestral range. For any particular ancestral range (a row), there are one or more possible descendant pairs of left,right ranges. If a particular cell is blank, that means that event has weight 0 and therefore probability 0 in the final calculation.

These figures and captions will look a little different in the final, there were some changes in proof. Cheers!
Nick

 
Yours sincerely,
Roger Billig
